p: Plenty of people are a bit nervous before their first go at full-body VR, so here are the common questions answered. Worried about feeling queasy? Because you're physically walking around rather than gliding about with a joystick, lots of people find free-roam VR more comfortable than home headsets, though if you're prone to motion sickness it's still wise to mention it to the staff. Wear glasses? Let the team know so they can help you get a comfortable fit.

Worried about bumping into walls or your mates? The system tracks everyone in the room, so you'll see your teammates as avatars, and the staff keep an eye on things from outside. Just follow the safety briefing and you'll quickly forget you're in a room at all. Not a gamer? Don't worry. The controls are simple, and some of the best players are people who've never picked up a console in their lives.

Westfield London is a handy base because there's so much else around it. The centre itself has a huge choice of restaurants, so planning a meal before or after is easy. Shepherd's Bush Empire, the famous music venue, is just across the green, and Loftus Road, home of Queens Park Rangers, is a short walk away.

If you fancy some fresh air, Holland Park is a short Tube or bus ride away, with woodland walks, peacocks strutting about and the peaceful Kyoto Garden, a beautiful Japanese garden with a waterfall and koi carp. Notting Hill and Portobello Road Market are also close by, perfect for a Saturday wander among the antiques stalls and colourful houses. With the Central line and the Hammersmith & City and Circle lines all nearby, getting there and home again is easy.
